sanskrit: prahāyobhayam apy etaj jñānaṃ karma ca kevalam tṛtīyeyaṃ samākhyātā niṣṭhā tena mahātmanā
english: Renouncing both of these alike—pure knowledge and action—that great-souled one has declared this third as the firm ground of consummation.

sanskrit: yame ca niyame caiva dveṣe kāme parigrahe māne dambhe tathā snehe sadṛśās te kuṭumbibhiḥ
english: In restraint and observance, in hatred, desire, and possession, in pride, hypocrisy, and likewise affection, those ascetics are no different from householders.

sanskrit: tridaṇḍādiṣu yady asti mokṣo jñānena kena cit chatrādiṣu kathaṃ na syāt tulyahetau parigrahe
english: If liberation comes through some knowledge while one yet holds the triple staff and the rest, why should it not come amid parasols and such, the cause of attachment being equal?

sanskrit: yena yena hi yasyārthaḥ kāraṇeneha kasya cit tat tad ālambate dravyaṃ sarvaḥ sve sve parigrahe
english: For whatever object serves a man's purpose, for whatever reason, that very thing he clings to—each to his own possessions.

sanskrit: doṣadarśī tu gārhasthye yo vrajaty āśramāntaram utsṛjan parigṛhṇaṃś ca so 'pi saṅgān na mucyate
english: He who, seeing fault in the householder's life, passes to another stage—renouncing one thing while grasping another—he too is not freed from attachments.

sanskrit: ādhipatye tathā tulye nigrahānugrahātmani rājarṣibhikṣukācāryā mucyante kena hetunā
english: When their sovereignty is alike, its essence the power to punish and to favor, by what cause are royal sage, mendicant, and teacher set free?

sanskrit: atha satyādhipatye 'pi jñānenaiveha kevalam mucyante kiṃ na mucyante pade paramake sthitāḥ
english: And if even amid real lordship men are freed here by knowledge alone, why should those who abide established in the supreme state not be freed?

sanskrit: kāṣāyadhāraṇaṃ mauṇḍyaṃ triviṣṭabdhaḥ kamaṇḍaluḥ liṅgāny atyartham etāni na mokṣāyeti me matiḥ
english: The wearing of ochre robes, the shaven head, the triple staff held upright, the water-pot—these outward signs serve excessively little for liberation: such is my view.

sanskrit: yadi saty api liṅge 'smiñ jñānam evātra kāraṇam nirmokṣāyeha duḥkhasya liṅgamātraṃ nirarthakam
english: If, even when this badge is present, knowledge alone is the cause here of release from suffering, then the mere badge is without purpose.

sanskrit: atha vā duḥkhaśaithilyaṃ vīkṣya liṅge kṛtā matiḥ kiṃ tad evārthasāmānyaṃ chatrādiṣu na lakṣyate
english: Or if, seeing some slackening of suffering, one's mind is set upon the badge—why is that same common benefit not to be discerned amid parasols and the rest?

sanskrit: ākiṃcanye na mokṣo 'sti kaiṃcanye nāsti bandhanam kaiṃcanye cetare caiva jantur jñānena mucyate
english: In utter destitution there is no liberation; in having something there is no bondage; whether having something or not, the creature is freed by knowledge.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmārthakāmeṣu tathā rājyaparigrahe bandhanāyataneṣv eṣu viddhy abandhe pade sthitam
english: Therefore, amid dharma, wealth, and desire, and likewise the holding of a kingdom—in these abodes of bondage—know me to stand established in the state where no bond is.

sanskrit: rājyaiśvaryamayaḥ pāśaḥ snehāyatanabandhanaḥ mokṣāśmaniśiteneha chinnas tyāgāsinā mayā
english: The noose made of royal dominion, the fetter that is the abode of affection—here I have cut it with the sword of renunciation, whetted upon the stone of liberation.

sanskrit: so 'ham evaṃgato mukto jātāsthas tvayi bhikṣuki ayathārtho hi te varṇo vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tan mama
english: I, having come to this state, am free; yet I have grown wary of you, O mendicant woman, for your guise is false—I shall tell you why; hear that from me.

sanskrit: saukumāryaṃ tathā rūpaṃ vapur agryaṃ tathā vayaḥ tavaitāni samastāni niyamaś ceti saṃśayaḥ
english: Your delicacy, your beauty, your superb body, and your youth—all these together, set beside your ascetic discipline, breed doubt.

sanskrit: yac cāpy ananurūpaṃ te liṅgasyāsya viceṣṭitam mukto 'yaṃ syān na vety asmād dharṣito matparigrahaḥ
english: And since your conduct ill befits this badge you wear, my retinue has been thrown into agitation, wondering whether this one be liberated or not.

sanskrit: na ca kāmasamāyukte mukte 'py asti tridaṇḍakam na rakṣyate tvayā cedaṃ na muktasyāsti gopanā
english: In one yoked to desire there is no triple staff, even were such a one freed; and you do not keep this discipline—yet for the liberated there is nothing to conceal.

sanskrit: matpakṣasaṃśrayāc cāyaṃ śṛṇu yas te vyatikramaḥ āśrayantyāḥ svabhāvena mama pūrvaparigraham
english: And hear too this transgression of yours, arising from your resort to my side—you who by your own nature have entered into what is already mine.

sanskrit: praveśas te kṛtaḥ kena mama rāṣṭre pure tathā kasya vā saṃnisargāt tvaṃ praviṣṭā hṛdayaṃ mama
english: By whom was your entry made into my realm and my city? And by whose leave have you entered into my very heart?

sanskrit: varṇapravaramukhyāsi brāhmaṇī kṣatriyo hy aham nāvayor ekayogo 'sti mā kṛthā varṇasaṃkaram
english: You are foremost of the highest class, a brāhmaṇa woman, while I am a kṣatriya; there is no joining of us two—do not work a confusion of the orders.

sanskrit: vartase mokṣadharmeṣu gārhasthye tv aham āśrame ayaṃ cāpi sukaṣṭas te dvitīyo ''śramasaṃkaraḥ
english: You dwell in the duties of liberation, while I am in the householder's stage; this is your second grievous fault—a confounding of the stages of life.

sanskrit: sagotrāṃ vāsagotrāṃ vā na veda tvāṃ na vettha mām sagotram āviśantyās te tṛtīyo gotrasaṃkaraḥ
english: Whether of my lineage or of another, I do not know you, nor do you know me; in entering one of the same lineage lies your third fault—a confounding of clans.

sanskrit: atha jīvati te bhartā proṣito 'py atha vā kva cit agamyā parabhāryeti caturtho dharmasaṃkaraḥ
english: And if your husband yet lives, though abroad or somewhere away—another man's wife is not to be approached: this is the fourth, a confounding of right.

sanskrit: sā tvam etāny akāryāṇi kāryāpekṣā vyavasyasi avijñānena vā yuktā mithyājñānena vā punaḥ
english: You, then, with an eye to some end, undertake these things that ought not be done—whether possessed of mere ignorance, or again of false knowledge.

sanskrit: atha vāpi svatantrāsi svadoṣeṇeha kena cit yadi kiṃ cic chrutaṃ te 'sti sarvaṃ kṛtam anarthakam
english: Or else you act on your own authority, through some fault of your own; and if you possess any learning at all, you have rendered it wholly useless.

sanskrit: idam anyat tṛtīyaṃ te bhāvasparśavighātakam duṣṭāyā lakṣyate liṅgaṃ pravaktavyaṃ prakāśitam
english: This is yet a third thing of yours, frustrating the touch of true intent: the badge of a corrupt woman is plain to see, and must be openly declared.

sanskrit: na mayy evābhisaṃdhis te jayaiṣiṇyā jaye kṛtaḥ yeyaṃ matpariṣat kṛtsnā jetum icchasi tām api
english: Your design, in your longing for victory, was not set upon conquering me alone; this whole assembly of mine too you wish to conquer.

sanskrit: tathā hy evaṃ punaś ca tvaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ svāṃ pratimuñcasi matpakṣapratighātāya svapakṣodbhāvanāya ca
english: For thus, again and again, you let loose your own doctrine—to strike down my position and to set up your own.

sanskrit: sā svenāmarṣajena tvam ṛddhimohena mohitā bhūyaḥ sṛjasi yogāstraṃ viṣāmṛtam ivaikadhā
english: You, bewildered by the delusion born of your own impatience for mastery, again loose the weapon of yoga, like poison and nectar mingled into one.

sanskrit: icchator hi dvayor lābhaḥ strīpuṃsor amṛtopamaḥ alābhaś cāpy araktasya so 'tra doṣo viṣopamaḥ
english: For when both desire it, the union of woman and man is like nectar; but the failure of it, for one who feels no passion, is here a flaw like poison.

sanskrit: mā sprākṣīḥ sadhu jānīṣva svaśāstram anupālaya kṛteyaṃ hi vijijñāsā mukto neti tvayā mama etat sarvaṃ praticchannaṃ mayi nārhasi gūhitum
english: Touch me not; know rightly; keep faithful to your own teaching. This examination has been made by you—whether I am liberated or not—and all this, concealed within me, you ought not to hide from me.

sanskrit: sā yadi tvaṃ svakāryeṇa yady anyasya mahīpateḥ tattvaṃ satrapraticchannā mayi nārhasi gūhitum
english: Whether you act for your own purpose or for that of some other king, the truth—disguised under a pious pretext—you ought not to hide from me.

sanskrit: na rājānaṃ mṛṣā gacchen na dvijātiṃ kathaṃ cana na striyaṃ strīguṇopetāṃ hanyur hy ete mṛṣāgatāḥ
english: None should approach a king with falsehood, nor a brāhmaṇa in any wise, nor a woman endowed with womanly virtues; for these, falsely approached, can destroy.

sanskrit: rājñāṃ hi balam aiśvaryaṃ brahma brahmavidāṃ balam rūpayauvanasaubhāgyaṃ strīṇāṃ balam anuttamam
english: For the strength of kings is their dominion; the strength of those who know the sacred is the sacred itself; beauty, youth, and good fortune are the unsurpassed strength of women.

sanskrit: ata etair balair ete balinaḥ svārtham icchatā ārjavenābhigantavyā vināśāya hy anārjavam
english: Mighty therefore by these strengths, such ones must be approached with straightforwardness by him who seeks his own good; for crookedness leads to ruin.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ jātiṃ śrutaṃ vṛttaṃ bhāvaṃ prakṛtim ātmanaḥ kṛtyam āgamane caiva vaktum arhasi tattvataḥ
english: You, then, ought to tell me truly your birth, your learning, your conduct, your intent, your nature, and your errand in coming.

sanskrit: ity etair asukhair vākyair ayuktair asamañjasaiḥ pratyādiṣṭā narendreṇa sulabhā na vyakampata
english: Thus rebuked by the king with these unpleasant, unjust, and ill-ordered words, Sulabhā was not shaken.

sanskrit: uktavākye tu nṛpatau sulabhā cārudarśanā tataś cārutaraṃ vākyaṃ pracakrāmātha bhāṣitum
english: When the king had finished speaking, the fair-faced Sulabhā then set herself to utter words still fairer.

sanskrit: navabhir navabhiś caiva doṣair vāgbuddhidūṣaṇaiḥ apetam upapannārtham aṣṭādaśaguṇānvitam
english: Free from the eighteen faults—nine and nine again—that vitiate speech and understanding, well furnished with meaning and endowed with the eighteen merits:

sanskrit: saukṣmyaṃ saṃkhyākramau cobhau nirṇayaḥ saprayojanaḥ pañcaitāny arthajātāni vākyam ity ucyate nṛpa
english: Subtlety, enumeration, and sequence—these two—decision, and purpose: these five orders of meaning together are called a true utterance, O king.

sanskrit: eṣām ekaikaśo 'rthānāṃ saukṣmyādīnāṃ sulakṣaṇam śṛṇu saṃsāryamāṇānāṃ padārthaiḥ padavākyataḥ
english: Hear the proper mark of each one of these meanings—subtlety and the rest—as they are set forth in due order through the senses of words, word by word and sentence by sentence.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ jñeyeṣu bhinneṣu yathābhedena vartate tatrātiśayinī buddhis tat saukṣmyam iti vartate
english: When, among distinct objects of knowledge, cognition proceeds according to their distinctions, there the surpassing keenness of the intellect operates as what is called subtlety.

sanskrit: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca pramāṇaṃ pravibhāgaśaḥ kaṃ cid artham abhipretya sā saṃkhyety upadhāryatām
english: The measuring out of faults and merits, severally and apart, with some particular aim in view—that is to be understood as enumeration.

sanskrit: idaṃ pūrvam idaṃ paścād vaktavyaṃ yad vivakṣitam kramayogaṃ tam apy āhur vākyaṃ vākyavido janāḥ
english: "This is to be said first, this afterward"—the ordering of what one means to express: that too those who know speech call the conjunction of sequence within an utterance.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu pratijñāya viśeṣataḥ idaṃ tad iti vākyānte procyate sa vinirṇayaḥ
english: Having made a particular proposition concerning dharma, wealth, desire, or liberation, that which is declared at the close of the speech as "this is that" is the decision.

sanskrit: icchādveṣabhavair duḥkhaiḥ prakarṣo yatra jāyate tatra yā nṛpate vṛttis tat prayojanam iṣyate
english: Where, through the sufferings born of desire and aversion, some impulse arises, the activity that follows there, O king, is held to be the purpose.

sanskrit: tāny etāni yathoktāni saukṣmyādīni janādhipa ekārthasamavetāni vākyaṃ mama niśāmaya
english: These, then, just as stated—subtlety and the rest, O lord of men—joined together upon a single meaning: mark well my utterance.

sanskrit: upetārtham abhinnārthaṃ nāpavṛttaṃ na cādhikam nāślakṣṇaṃ na ca saṃdigdhaṃ vakṣyāmi paramaṃ tava
english: Furnished with meaning, undivided in meaning, neither digressive nor excessive, not rough, not doubtful—such supreme speech shall I utter to you.

sanskrit: na gurvakṣarasaṃbaddhaṃ parāṅmukhamukhaṃ na ca nānṛtaṃ na trivargeṇa viruddhaṃ nāpy asaṃskṛtam
english: Not cumbered with heavy syllables, nor turned away from its subject, not false, not opposed to the three aims, nor uncultivated;

sanskrit: na nyūnaṃ kaṣṭaśabdaṃ vā vyutkramābhihitaṃ na ca na śeṣaṃ nānukalpena niṣkāraṇam ahetukam
english: not deficient, nor of harsh words, nor uttered out of order, not left incomplete, nor by way of mere makeshift, not causeless nor without ground.

sanskrit: kāmāt krodhād bhayāl lobhād dainyād ānāryakāt tathā hrīto 'nukrośato mānān na vakṣyāmi kathaṃ cana
english: Out of desire, anger, fear, greed, abjectness, or baseness, out of shame, pity, or pride—from none of these shall I speak in any wise.

sanskrit: vaktā śrotā ca vākyaṃ ca yadā tv avikalaṃ nṛpa samam eti vivakṣāyāṃ tadā so 'rthaḥ prakāśate
english: When speaker, listener, and speech, O king, come together unimpaired and matched in the intent to convey, then that meaning shines forth.

sanskrit: vaktavye tu yadā vaktā śrotāram avamanyate svārtham āha parārthaṃ vā tadā vākyaṃ na rohati
english: But when, in what is to be spoken, the speaker holds the listener in contempt, declaring his own meaning or another's, then the speech does not take root.

sanskrit: atha yaḥ svārtham utsṛjya parārthaṃ prāha mānavaḥ viśaṅkā jāyate tasmin vākyaṃ tad api doṣavat
english: And when a man, abandoning his own meaning, declares another's, mistrust arises toward him, and that speech too is faulty.

sanskrit: yas tu vaktā dvayor artham aviruddhaṃ prabhāṣate śrotuś caivātmanaś caiva sa vaktā netaro nṛpa
english: But the speaker who declares a meaning unopposed to both—to the listener's and to his own—he is the true speaker, no other, O king.

sanskrit: tad arthavad idaṃ vākyam upetaṃ vākyasaṃpadā avikṣiptamanā rājann ekāgraḥ śrotum arhasi
english: This speech of mine, then, full of meaning and endowed with the perfections of utterance, you ought to hear, O king, with mind undistracted and intent.

sanskrit: kāsi kasya kuto veti tvayāham abhicoditā tatrottaram idaṃ vākyaṃ rājann ekamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: "Who are you, whose, and whence?"—thus you have challenged me; to that, hear this answer of mine, O king, with single mind.

sanskrit: yathā jatu ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca pāṃsavaś codabindubhiḥ suśliṣṭāni tathā rājan prāṇinām iha saṃbhavaḥ
english: As lac and wood and grains of dust are closely held together by drops of water, even so, O king, is the coming-to-be of living creatures here.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśo raso rūpaṃ gandhaḥ pañcendriyāṇi ca pṛthag ātmā daśātmānaḥ saṃśliṣṭā jatukāṣṭhavat
english: Sound, touch, taste, form, and smell; the five sense-faculties; and the self apart—these ten realities are bound together like lac and wood.

sanskrit: na caiṣāṃ codanā kā cid astīty eṣa viniścayaḥ ekaikasyeha vijñānaṃ nāsty ātmani tathā pare
english: Among these there is no prompting of one by another—this is the settled conclusion; here no single one has cognition of itself or of another.

sanskrit: na veda cakṣuś cakṣuṣṭvaṃ śrotraṃ nātmani vartate tathaiva vyabhicāreṇa na vartante parasparam saṃśliṣṭā nābhijāyante yathāpa iha pāṃsavaḥ
english: The eye does not know its own eye-hood, nor does hearing turn upon itself; and likewise they do not act upon one another by deviation; though bound together, they do not arise from one another, as grains of dust do not from water here.

sanskrit: bāhyān anyān apekṣante guṇāṃs tān api me śṛṇu rūpaṃ cakṣuḥ prakāśaś ca darśane hetavas trayaḥ yathaivātra tathānyeṣu jñānajñeyeṣu hetavaḥ
english: They depend on other, external factors—hear those too from me: form, the eye, and light are the three causes of seeing; and just as here, so in the other cases the causes of cognition and its objects hold.

sanskrit: jñānajñeyāntare tasmin mano nāmāparo guṇaḥ vicārayati yenāyaṃ niścaye sādhvasādhunī
english: In that interval between cognition and its object there is another factor named mind, by which this being deliberates, in deciding, upon what is right and what is wrong.

sanskrit: dvādaśas tv aparas tatra buddhir nāma guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ yena saṃśayapūrveṣu boddhavyeṣu vyavasyati
english: And there a twelfth, another factor named intellect, is remembered, by which one comes to resolution upon things to be understood that were first beset with doubt.

sanskrit: atha dvādaśake tasmin sattvaṃ nāmāparo guṇaḥ mahāsattvo 'lpasattvo vā jantur yenānumīyate
english: Then, beyond that twelfth, another factor named disposition, by which a creature is inferred to be of great spirit or of little.

sanskrit: kṣetrajña iti cāpy anyo guṇas tatra caturdaśaḥ mamāyam iti yenāyaṃ manyate na ca manyate
english: And the knower-of-the-field is yet another, the fourteenth factor there, by which one thinks "this is mine," and again thinks it not.

sanskrit: atha pañcadaśo rājan guṇas tatrāparaḥ smṛtaḥ pṛthak kalāsamūhasya sāmagryaṃ tad ihocyate
english: Then a fifteenth, O king, another factor there is remembered: the gathering into wholeness of the aggregate of parts otherwise separate—that is here so called.

sanskrit: guṇas tv evāparas tatra saṃghāta iti ṣoḍaśaḥ ākṛtir vyaktir ity etau guṇau yasmin samāśritau
english: And yet another factor there, the combination, is the sixteenth, in which these two factors—shape and manifest form—are conjoined.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe jarāmṛtyū lābhālābhau priyāpriye iti caikonaviṃśo 'yaṃ dvaṃdvayoga iti smṛtaḥ
english: Pleasure and pain, old age and death, gain and loss, the pleasant and the unpleasant—this, the nineteenth, is remembered as the conjunction of opposites.

sanskrit: ūrdhvam ekonaviṃśatyāḥ kālo nāmāparo guṇaḥ itīmaṃ viddhi viṃśatyā bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayam
english: Above the nineteen there is another factor named time; know thereby, in these twenty, the arising and passing-away of beings.

sanskrit: viṃśakaś caiṣa saṃghāto mahābhūtāni pañca ca sadasadbhāvayogau ca guṇāv anyau prakāśakau
english: This combination of twenty, and the five great elements, and the conjunction of being and non-being—these are two further illuminating factors.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ viṃśatiś caiva guṇāḥ sapta ca ye smṛtāḥ vidhiḥ śukraṃ balaṃ ceti traya ete guṇāḥ pare
english: Thus the twenty-seven factors that are remembered; and ordinance, generative seed, and force—these three are yet further factors.

sanskrit: ekaviṃśaś ca daśa ca kalāḥ saṃkhyānataḥ smṛtāḥ samagrā yatra vartante tac charīram iti smṛtam
english: Thirty parts in all are remembered by enumeration; that wherein they all together subsist is remembered as the body.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ prakṛtiṃ tv āsāṃ kalānāṃ kaś cid icchati vyaktaṃ cāsāṃ tathaivānyaḥ sthūladarśī prapaśyati
english: As the unmanifest source of these parts some hold their nature to be; while another, of grosser sight, beholds their manifest form alone.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ yadi vā vyaktaṃ dvayīm atha catuṣṭayīm prakṛtiṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ paśyanty adhyātmacintakāḥ
english: Whether unmanifest or manifest, twofold or fourfold, the nature of all beings—so the meditators on the inmost self behold it.

sanskrit: seyaṃ prakṛtir avyaktā kalābhir vyaktatāṃ gatā ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca rājendra ye cāpy anye śarīriṇaḥ
english: This very nature, unmanifest, comes through its parts to manifestation—I and you, O lord of kings, and all others that are embodied.

sanskrit: bindunyāsādayo 'vasthāḥ śukraśoṇitasaṃbhavāḥ yāsām eva nipātena kalalaṃ nāma jāyate
english: The states beginning with the deposit of the drop, arising from seed and blood—by the very falling-together of which there comes to be what is called the embryonic film.

sanskrit: kalalād arbudotpattiḥ peśī cāpy arbudodbhavā peśyās tv aṅgābhinirvṛttir nakharomāṇi cāṅgataḥ
english: From the film arises the swelling mass, and from the mass the fleshy lump; from the lump the formation of limbs, and from the limbs the nails and hairs.

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇe navame māse jantor jātasya maithila jāyate nāmarūpatvaṃ strī pumān veti liṅgataḥ
english: When the ninth month is full and the creature is born, O king of Mithilā, name-and-form comes to be, marked as woman or man by its sign.

sanskrit: jātamātraṃ tu tad rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāmranakhāṅguli kaumārarūpam āpannaṃ rūpato nopalabhyate
english: But that form just newly born, seen with its copper-hued nails and fingers, once it has assumed the form of childhood, is no longer recognized by its earlier shape.
